left: The poop is on the left side of the frame. Place the gas-mask pigeon between the poop and the left edge of the frame. Place the curious pigeon, the equipment case, and the camera on the right side of the poop, using the open space on the right to balance the composition.
right: The poop is on the right side of the frame. Place the gas-mask pigeon between the poop and the right edge of the frame. Place the curious pigeon, the equipment case, and the camera on the left side of the poop, using the open space on the left to balance the composition.
middle:
ACCIDENT SCENE. The poop is near the middle of the frame, and the investigation has gone wrong. Where this conflicts with the poses, gas-mask rules, or gaze rules in sections 2, 5, 6, 11, 12, and 14, this section wins.

The Hazardous-Material Specialist has been overcome. It lies on its back on the pavement on the left side of the poop, wings slightly splayed and feet in the air, as though it has passed out. Its body is aligned in one straight line from tail to beak: back flat on the pavement, breast and belly facing up, both feet rising from the belly, and the neck extending straight out from the shoulders, never curled under the body or turned to one side. The back of its head rests flat on the pavement, its neck lying limp along the ground, with the beak pointing straight up at the sky and its eyes closed. The head is not lifted, and it is never twisted, turned face-down, or bent at an unnatural angle. It looks unconscious, not injured: no blood, no visible harm, feathers intact, still wearing its yellow vest. Its gas mask has come off and lies on the pavement nearby, between the bird and the poop.

The equipment line (the case, the camera on its tripod, and the detector) sits on the right side of the poop. The Curious Investigator has left its post: it stands in front of the equipment line, closer to the camera, caught mid-stride toward the viewer, and looks directly into the lens, as though walking up to report the incident. Its pose and expression stay natural and pigeon-like, never human.

The poop stays clearly visible in the middle, inside the evidence markers.
